pages.text: The next day, {hero} and {pet} walked to Candy Village. The houses were made of cake, and the roofs were [[covered|with something all over the top]] in pink icing. The whole village smelled sweeter than a birthday party.

q.q: What were the roofs covered in?
q.explain: “The roofs were covered in pink icing.”

pages.text: In the market they met Mrs Toffee, the baker. She looked [[worried|unhappy because you think something bad may happen]]. “Someone took my best cake last night,” she said. “And I found this strange paper next to my oven.” It was the second page!

q.explain: “Someone took my best cake last night.”

pages.text: The page had a [[clue|something that helps you find an answer]] on it: “Follow the crumbs.” {hero} looked down. There was a line of tiny cake crumbs on the road. It went past the school and into the park.

q.q: What did the clue tell them to do?

pages.text: In the park they found a very small dragon. It was eating the cake. “Sorry!” it said. “I was so hungry.” Mrs Toffee [[laughed|made a happy sound because something was funny]]. “Next time, just ask! I'm going to bake you your own cake.” {hero} put the page in the book.

q.q: What is Mrs Toffee going to do?
q.explain: “I'm going to bake you your own cake.” — going to = a plan.

final.q: In the story, a “clue” is something that…
final.explain: A clue helps you find the answer to a mystery.
